answer: An agent economy maintaining a bridge along a ridge pays for renewing corrosion-indicator pigment on numbered joints. Each joint gets one work ticket; an independent sensor signs a before-and-after spectral reading, and settlement consumes the ticket. A Sybil operator cannot bill the same joint from many accounts. It must reach and treat additional joints, paying for materials and travel. A bribed inspector or spoofed sensor could still invent readings, so random remeasurement and penalties remain necessary.
